Docs / API Surface
Stackyard API Surface

Services and Endpoints

Base URL is the Stackyard listener (default http://localhost:4566). AWS-compatible services require SigV4 signing and use standard AWS headers.

For the new docs experience, see Stackyard Web Docs: AWS Services.

Core

Health and debugging endpoints.

Auth: none
Supported Actions

Action Type: HTTP request action

Method Path Description
GET /_stackyard/health Service status payload.
GET /_stackyard/debug/request Echoes method, headers, and query string.

  7. Stage 6: Implement tagging and resource-arn flows for TagResource, UntagResource, and GetTags. (implemented)
  8. Stage 7: Add docs/examples/coverage wiring and validate zero NotImplemented responses across all catalog actions. (implemented)

AWS AppConfig

SigV4 signed with service appconfig. REST JSON API over AppConfig resources such as POST /applications, GET /applications/{ApplicationId}, and POST /applications/{ApplicationId}/environments/{EnvironmentId}/deployments. Current behavior defines the staged implementation plan and catalog coverage across all 45 documented actions and 18 documented API data types.

SigV4: appconfig API: REST JSON
Staged Plan
  1. Stage 0: Route wiring, SigV4 validation, operation/type catalog registration, and baseline response envelopes for known AppConfig routes.
  2. Stage 1: Application and environment lifecycle APIs, including create/get/list/update/delete semantics.
  3. Stage 2: Configuration profile and hosted configuration version lifecycle coverage with retrieval and listing behavior.
  4. Stage 3: Deployment strategy APIs and deployment execution lifecycle for start/get/list/stop flows.
  5. Stage 4: Extension and extension-association management, including create/list/get/update/delete operations.
  6. Stage 5: Validation and account settings surfaces for ValidateConfiguration, GetAccountSettings, and UpdateAccountSettings.
  7. Stage 6: Resource tagging and ARN normalization behavior for TagResource, UntagResource, and ListTagsForResource.
  8. Stage 7: Coverage pre-seeding/dependency ordering, contract hardening, docs finalization, and runnable examples with no NotImplemented responses.

Amazon AppFlow

SigV4 signed with service appflow. AppFlow exposes a REST/JSON API over resource routes such as POST /create-flow, POST /start-flow, and GET /tags/{resourceArn}. Current behavior defines the staged implementation plan and catalog coverage across all 25 documented actions and 151 documented API data types.

SigV4: appflow API: REST JSON
Staged Plan
  1. Stage 0: Add AppFlow REST router skeleton with SigV4 validation for appflow, operation/type catalogs, and baseline validation error envelopes. (implemented)
  2. Stage 1: Implement flow lifecycle/read/list APIs (CreateFlow, UpdateFlow, DeleteFlow, DescribeFlow, ListFlows) with deterministic seeded flow resources. (implemented)
  3. Stage 2: Implement flow execution APIs (StartFlow, StopFlow, CancelFlowExecutions, DescribeFlowExecutionRecords) with deterministic execution history snapshots. (implemented)
  4. Stage 3: Implement connector profile lifecycle/read/list APIs (CreateConnectorProfile, UpdateConnectorProfile, DeleteConnectorProfile, DescribeConnectorProfiles). (implemented)
  5. Stage 4: Implement connector metadata/entity discovery APIs (DescribeConnector, DescribeConnectors, DescribeConnectorEntity, ListConnectorEntities, ListConnectors). (implemented)
  6. Stage 5: Implement private/custom connector registration APIs (RegisterConnector, UpdateConnectorRegistration, UnregisterConnector, ResetConnectorMetadataCache). (implemented)
  7. Stage 6: Implement resource tagging semantics (TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsForResource) with ARN normalization and deterministic tag state. (implemented)
  8. Stage 7: Integrate docs/examples/coverage harness wiring (aliases, raw fallback route extraction, signing compatibility, placeholder hydration) and verify no AppFlow action returns NotImplemented. (implemented)

AWS Data Pipeline

SigV4 signed with service datapipeline. Data Pipeline exposes an AWS JSON 1.1 API over POST / with X-Amz-Target: DataPipeline.<Action>. Staged implementation coverage is complete across all 19 documented actions and 15 documented API data types.

SigV4: datapipeline API: AWS JSON 1.1
Staged Plan
  1. Stage 0: Add Data Pipeline JSON router skeleton with SigV4 validation for datapipeline, target parsing for DataPipeline.<Action>, operation/type catalogs, and baseline validation envelopes. (implemented)
  2. Stage 1: Implement pipeline lifecycle and tagging APIs (CreatePipeline, DeletePipeline, ActivatePipeline, DeactivatePipeline, AddTags, RemoveTags, ListPipelines, DescribePipelines) with deterministic in-memory state. (implemented)
  3. Stage 2: Implement definition/object APIs (PutPipelineDefinition, GetPipelineDefinition, ValidatePipelineDefinition, QueryObjects, DescribeObjects, EvaluateExpression) with deterministic object persistence. (implemented)
  4. Stage 3: Implement task-runner APIs (PollForTask, ReportTaskProgress, ReportTaskRunnerHeartbeat, SetTaskStatus, SetStatus) with deterministic task-state transitions. (implemented)
  5. Stage 4: Add stage-0 and stage-1..6 test coverage for catalog completeness, lifecycle/read surfaces, validation errors, and idempotency behavior. (implemented)
  6. Stage 5: Add Docker examples (datapipeline-basic, datapipeline-advanced) covering signed JSON-RPC requests and multi-action lifecycle flows. (implemented)
  7. Stage 6: Integrate Python coverage harness fallback routing/payload generation for Data Pipeline and verify all actions return non-NotImplemented responses. (implemented)

  7. Stage 6: Implement association/tagging/search/idempotency surfaces (Associate*/Disassociate*, TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsForResource, Search*) with stricter validation and error-parity hardening.
  8. Stage 7: Integrate docs/examples/coverage harness wiring (aliases, raw fallback route extraction, placeholder hydration, signing compatibility) and verify no Connect action returns NotImplemented.

AWS Control Catalog

Planned SigV4 service is controlcatalog. API operations are expected over AWS Control Catalog control-plane endpoints with SigV4 signing. This staged plan targets all 6 documented actions and 23 documented API data types.

SigV4: controlcatalog API: Control Plane
Staged Plan
  1. Stage 0: Add service routing skeleton, SigV4 validation, operation/type catalog wiring, and baseline unknown-action error envelopes.
  2. Stage 1: Implement ListControls and GetControl with deterministic control metadata, implementation details, and control parameter shapes.
  3. Stage 2: Implement domain and objective discovery APIs (ListDomains, ListObjectives) with stable pagination behavior and filter handling.
  4. Stage 3: Implement control mapping surfaces (ListControlMappings, ListCommonControls) and relationship projections for framework/common-control associations.
  5. Stage 4: Add robust request validation and AWS-style error mapping for unsupported filters, malformed identifiers, and pagination contract violations.
  6. Stage 5: Add deterministic seeding and dependency ordering in coverage harness to ensure all catalog/list/get workflows execute against valid in-memory state.
  7. Stage 6: Harden response parity for shape fidelity, enum values, optional field behavior, and idempotent read patterns under repeated calls.
  8. Stage 7: Verify CI and endpoint coverage with no NotImplemented responses across all documented actions.

SigV4: controltower API: Control Plane

  2. Stage 1: Implement landing zone lifecycle APIs (CreateLandingZone, GetLandingZone, UpdateLandingZone, DeleteLandingZone, ResetLandingZone) with deterministic state transitions.

  6. Stage 5: Implement tagging APIs and read-only summaries, including drift and inheritance fields in shaped responses.
  7. Stage 6: Add pre-seeding and dependency ordering in the coverage harness so operations execute against valid landing-zone/baseline/control state.
  8. Stage 7: Harden contract parity (error types, validation, pagination/idempotency) and verify CI + endpoint coverage with no NotImplemented responses.

Amazon HealthImaging

SigV4 signed with service medical-imaging. REST JSON API over resource paths such as GET /datastore, GET /datastore/{datastoreId}, and POST /datastore/{datastoreId}/searchImageSets. Staged implementation coverage is complete across all 18 documented actions and 22 documented API data types.

SigV4: medical-imaging API: REST JSON
Staged Plan
  1. Stage 0: Route wiring, SigV4 validation, operation/type catalog registration, and baseline REST/JSON handler coverage. (implemented)
  2. Stage 1: Read/list/get coverage for datastores, DICOM import jobs, image frames, image sets, metadata, and version listing surfaces. (implemented)
  3. Stage 2: Datastore and DICOM import lifecycle create/start flows (CreateDatastore, StartDICOMImportJob) with deterministic persisted state. (implemented)
  4. Stage 3: Image set mutation lifecycle (CopyImageSet, DeleteImageSet, UpdateImageSetMetadata) with idempotency and status transition parity. (implemented)
  5. Stage 4: Tagging and resource metadata APIs (TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsForResource) plus datastore/image-set consistency checks. (implemented)
  6. Stage 5: Validation/error-model parity and pagination/filtering behavior for list/search operations, including edge-case contract tests. (implemented)
  7. Stage 6: Coverage pre-seeding and dependency ordering for datastore/image-set/import-job relationships to reduce precondition-tolerated runs. (implemented)
  8. Stage 7: Contract hardening, regression expansion, docs finalization, runnable healthimaging-basic/healthimaging-advanced examples, and coverage-script integration. (implemented)

Amazon HealthOmics

SigV4 signed with service omics. REST JSON API over mixed resource paths (for example POST /sequencestores, GET /workflow, and POST /run). Staged implementation coverage is complete across all 96 documented actions and 80 documented API data types.

SigV4: omics API: REST JSON
Staged Plan
  1. Stage 0: Route wiring, SigV4 validation, operation/type catalog registration, and baseline REST/JSON error envelopes. (implemented)
  2. Stage 1: Read/list/get coverage for stores, runs, workflows, references, read sets, jobs, shares, tags, and access policy surfaces. (implemented)
  3. Stage 2: Create/start APIs for stores, workflows, run groups, run caches, run execution, imports, exports, activation, multipart upload, and sharing. (implemented)
  4. Stage 3: Update and mutation APIs for stores, workflow versions, run groups/caches, tags, and S3 access policy persistence semantics. (implemented)
  5. Stage 4: Delete/cancel lifecycle APIs with idempotent behavior and consistent terminal states. (implemented)
  6. Stage 5: Multipart upload and bulk job workflows (CreateMultipartReadSetUpload, UploadReadSetPart, CompleteMultipartReadSetUpload, AbortMultipartReadSetUpload, and batch delete). (implemented)
  7. Stage 6: Documentation updates and runnable omics-basic / omics-advanced examples. (implemented)
  8. Stage 7: Coverage script integration and deterministic contract checks ensuring no NotImplemented responses for implemented endpoints. (implemented)

AWS Elastic Block Storage (EBS)

Planned SigV4 service is ebs. REST API over direct snapshot paths such as POST /snapshots, PUT /snapshots/{snapshotId}/blocks/{blockIndex}, and POST /snapshots/completion/{snapshotId}. This staged plan targets all 6 documented actions and 23 documented API data types.

SigV4: ebs API: REST JSON + binary blocks
Staged Plan
  1. Stage 0: Add EBS Direct REST router skeleton with SigV4 validation for ebs, action/type catalog wiring, and baseline non-NotImplemented validation/error envelopes.
  2. Stage 1: Implement snapshot lifecycle foundation with StartSnapshot and CompleteSnapshot, deterministic snapshot IDs, and completion state transitions.
  3. Stage 2: Implement block write/read surfaces with PutSnapshotBlock and GetSnapshotBlock, including checksum fields and block token semantics.
  4. Stage 3: Implement block listing and delta APIs (ListSnapshotBlocks, ListChangedBlocks) with stable ordering and pagination tokens.
  5. Stage 4: Add AWS-style validation/error typing for snapshot/block indexes, token mismatches, and checksum constraints plus deterministic throttling conflict responses.
  6. Stage 5: Add dependency-aware pre-seeding and coverage hardening so all EBS Direct actions return non-NotImplemented responses under contract tests.

SigV4: iot API: REST JSON
Staged Plan
  1. Stage 0: Service scaffolding, SigV4 routing for iot, operation and type catalog registration, and baseline dependency/error envelopes.
  2. Stage 1: Core registry and grouping lifecycle APIs for things, thing types, thing groups, billing groups, and attributes/tagging read-models.
  3. Stage 2: Identity and policy surfaces including certificate/CA lifecycle, policy versioning, principal attachment workflows, and role alias flows.
  4. Stage 3: Device job and rollout lifecycle APIs including templates, executions, scheduling, and package/deployment targeting dependencies.
  5. Stage 4: Rules, authorizers, domain configurations, destinations, and VPC endpoint/control-plane networking configuration APIs.
  6. Stage 5: Audit and security operations including audit tasks/findings, mitigation action workflows, detect/security-profile behavior, and related summaries.
  7. Stage 6: Package/version, command, and fleet-management surfaces including indexing, event configuration, SBOM association, and state pre-seeding.
  8. Stage 7: Full contract hardening: pagination/filter semantics, idempotency parity, dependency ordering, auth-path realism, and coverage stabilization.

AWS IoT Managed Integrations

SigV4 signed with service iotmanagedintegrations. REST JSON API over documented method/path routes. Stackyard implements staged coverage across all 83 documented actions and 62 documented API data types.

SigV4: iotmanagedintegrations API: REST JSON
Staged Plan
  1. Stage 0: Add IoT Managed Integrations REST router skeleton with SigV4 validation for iotmanagedintegrations, action/type catalog wiring, documented method+URI route matching, and baseline validation envelopes for malformed JSON and unknown routes. (implemented)
  2. Stage 1: Implement account association and connector lifecycle/read/list surfaces (CreateAccountAssociation, UpdateAccountAssociation, DeleteAccountAssociation, GetAccountAssociation, ListAccountAssociations, plus cloud connector CRUD and listing APIs). (implemented)
  3. Stage 2: Implement destination, credential locker, notification configuration, and event log configuration lifecycle/read/list surfaces with deterministic identifiers and idempotent updates. (implemented)
  4. Stage 3: Implement managed thing and schema surfaces, including lifecycle/read/list APIs, account-association registration/deregistration, metadata/state/capabilities reads, and connector command/event forwarding envelopes. (implemented)
  5. Stage 4: Implement OTA task, OTA task configuration, provisioning profile, and device discovery lifecycle/read/list surfaces including execution listing and connectivity/state supporting reads. (implemented)
  6. Stage 5: Implement configuration and control surfaces (Get/PutDefaultEncryptionConfiguration, Get/PutHubConfiguration, runtime log configuration APIs, custom endpoint registration/read, and account association refresh semantics). (implemented)
  7. Stage 6: Harden tagging, validation, idempotency, and pagination semantics; finalize docs/examples/coverage integration so all documented actions avoid NotImplemented. (implemented)

AWS IoT FleetWise

SigV4 signed with service iotfleetwise. AWS JSON 1.0 API over POST / with Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.0 and X-Amz-Target: IoTAutobahnControlPlane.<Action>. Current planning in Stackyard tracks staged implementation across all 57 documented actions and 72 documented API data types.

SigV4: iotfleetwise API: JSON RPC
Staged Plan
  1. Stage 0: Add IoT FleetWise JSON-RPC router skeleton with SigV4 validation for iotfleetwise, action/type catalog wiring, IoTAutobahnControlPlane.<Action> target parsing, and baseline validation envelopes for malformed JSON and unknown actions.
  2. Stage 1: Implement account registration and global settings surfaces (RegisterAccount, GetRegisterAccountStatus, PutLoggingOptions, GetLoggingOptions, PutEncryptionConfiguration, GetEncryptionConfiguration).
  3. Stage 2: Implement catalog and manifest lifecycle/read/list surfaces for signal catalogs, model manifests, and decoder manifests (create/import/get/list/update/delete plus node/interface/signal listing APIs).
  4. Stage 3: Implement fleet and vehicle lifecycle/read/list/association APIs (CreateFleet, UpdateFleet, DeleteFleet, CreateVehicle, UpdateVehicle, DeleteVehicle, batch create/update, and fleet-vehicle association APIs).
  5. Stage 4: Implement campaign and state template lifecycle/read/list APIs, plus campaign/vehicle status read surfaces and deterministic relationship handling.
  6. Stage 5: Implement tagging parity and cross-resource consistency (TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsForResource) with ARN normalization, overwrite semantics, and deterministic ordering.
  7. Stage 6: Harden validation/idempotency/pagination behavior and complete docs/examples/coverage harness integration so every documented action avoids NotImplemented.

Elastic Beanstalk

SigV4 signed with service elasticbeanstalk. Elastic Beanstalk uses the Query protocol over POST / with form-encoded parameters including Action=* and Version=2010-12-01. Stackyard tracks staged implementation across all 47 documented actions and 56 documented API data types.

SigV4: elasticbeanstalk API: Query
Staged Plan
  1. Stage 0: Add Elastic Beanstalk Query router skeleton with SigV4 validation for elasticbeanstalk, action/type catalogs, form decoding, and baseline validation/error envelopes for malformed requests and unknown actions.
  2. Stage 1: Implement application/application-version lifecycle and read surfaces (Create/Update/Delete/DescribeApplication*) plus account and operations-role association APIs.
  3. Stage 2: Implement environment and configuration lifecycle/read/list flows (Create/Update/TerminateEnvironment, template/configuration actions, events/info retrieval, and environment resources).
  4. Stage 3: Implement platform and stack surfaces (Create/Delete/Describe/ListPlatform*, ListAvailableSolutionStacks, CreateStorageLocation, and DNS availability checks).
  5. Stage 4: Implement managed-action and health flows (Describe/ApplyEnvironmentManagedAction*, DescribeEnvironmentHealth, DescribeInstancesHealth, and environment operation controls).
  6. Stage 5: Implement tagging and lifecycle policy controls (ListTagsForResource, UpdateTagsForResource, UpdateApplicationResourceLifecycle) with deterministic validation and idempotent mutation behavior.
  7. Stage 6: Finalize docs/examples/coverage harness integration and verify all documented Elastic Beanstalk actions are reachable with no NotImplemented responses.

AWS Cloud Map

SigV4 signed with service servicediscovery. JSON RPC API over POST / with Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.1 and X-Amz-Target: Route53AutoNaming_v20170314.<Action>. Staged implementation planning is mapped to all 30 documented actions and 37 documented API data types.

SigV4: servicediscovery API: JSON RPC
Staged Plan
  1. Stage 0: Add service routing skeleton, SigV4 validation, JSON target parsing, action/type catalog wiring, and baseline unknown-action error envelopes.
  2. Stage 1: Implement foundational read/list and discovery coverage (ListNamespaces, ListServices, ListOperations, GetNamespace, GetService, GetOperation, DiscoverInstances, DiscoverInstancesRevision).
  3. Stage 2: Implement namespace lifecycle APIs for HTTP/private/public namespaces (Create*, Update*, DeleteNamespace), including namespace metadata/state validation.
  4. Stage 3: Implement service lifecycle APIs (CreateService, UpdateService, DeleteService) plus service-attribute APIs (GetServiceAttributes, UpdateServiceAttributes, DeleteServiceAttributes).
  5. Stage 4: Implement instance and health workflows (RegisterInstance, DeregisterInstance, GetInstance, ListInstances, GetInstancesHealthStatus, UpdateInstanceCustomHealthStatus).
  6. Stage 5: Implement tagging and resource-shape parity (TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsForResource) and ARN validation across namespace/service resources.
  7. Stage 6: Add deterministic pre-seeding, dependency ordering, pagination/filter fidelity, and AWS-style validation/error mapping for contract-mode stability.
  8. Stage 7: Verify CI and endpoint coverage for Cloud Map with no NotImplemented responses across all documented actions.

Amazon CloudFront

SigV4 signed with service cloudfront. REST XML control-plane API over versioned URIs such as /2020-05-31/*. Staged implementation planning is mapped to all 168 documented actions and 208 documented API data types.

SigV4: cloudfront API: REST XML
Staged Plan
  1. Stage 0: Add CloudFront router skeleton with SigV4 validation, versioned URI dispatch (/2020-05-31/*), XML request/response envelope helpers, and baseline AWS-style error mapping.
  2. Stage 1: Implement read/list foundations for global account and distribution state (GetDistribution, GetDistributionConfig, ListDistributions, GetDistributionTenant, ListDistributionTenants, ListConflictingAliases, ListDomainConflicts).
  3. Stage 2: Implement distribution lifecycle and deployment workflows (CreateDistribution*, UpdateDistribution*, CopyDistribution, DeleteDistribution, CreateInvalidation, invalidation/history retrieval APIs).
  4. Stage 3: Implement cache/origin behavior policy families and control objects (CachePolicy, OriginRequestPolicy, ResponseHeadersPolicy, RealtimeLogConfig, monitoring subscriptions, and related list/get/update/delete actions).
  5. Stage 4: Implement security and keying primitives (PublicKey, KeyGroup, trusted signers/key-groups, signer APIs, field-level encryption configs/profiles, and IAM certificate integration).
  6. Stage 5: Implement origin-access and edge-compute workflows (CloudFrontOriginAccessIdentity, OriginAccessControl, Function, KeyValueStore, function publish/test, and key-value import/update/delete/list flows).
  7. Stage 6: Implement advanced multi-tenant/network capabilities and tenancy controls (DistributionTenant, web ACL association APIs, anycast IP lists, connection groups/functions, VPC origin APIs, continuous deployment policies, and SaaS manager controls).
  8. Stage 7: Add deterministic pre-seeding/dependency ordering, tag APIs, contract-mode schema parity, and CI/coverage gating so all CloudFront endpoints return non-NotImplemented responses.

AWS Direct Connect

SigV4 signed with service directconnect. AWS JSON 1.1 control-plane API over POST / using targets like OvertureService.<Action>. Staged implementation planning is mapped to all 63 documented actions and 29 documented API data types.

SigV4: directconnect API: AWS JSON 1.1
Staged Plan
  1. Stage 0: Add Direct Connect router skeleton with SigV4 validation for directconnect, JSON 1.1 target parsing (OvertureService.*), baseline request/response helpers, and AWS-style error envelope mapping.
  2. Stage 1: Implement foundational read/list APIs for inventory and topology visibility (DescribeConnections, DescribeInterconnects, DescribeLags, DescribeLocations, DescribeVirtualInterfaces, DescribeTags).
  3. Stage 2: Implement core lifecycle for physical links and bundles (CreateConnection, DeleteConnection, UpdateConnection, CreateInterconnect, CreateLag, association/disassociation operations).
  4. Stage 3: Implement virtual interface workflows and confirmations (Create*VirtualInterface, Allocate*VirtualInterface, Confirm*VirtualInterface, AssociateVirtualInterface, DeleteVirtualInterface, attribute updates).
  5. Stage 4: Implement Direct Connect Gateway domain and attachment workflows (Create/Update/DeleteDirectConnectGateway, association proposals, association/attachment describe calls, and acceptance paths).
  6. Stage 5: Implement advanced routing and security flows (Create/DeleteBGPPeer, MACsec key association/disassociation, LOA retrieval APIs, router configuration APIs, and BGP failover test lifecycle).
  7. Stage 6: Add deterministic pre-seeding and dependency ordering for connection/interconnect/LAG/VIF/gateway scenarios so coverage can execute full contracts with minimal precondition tolerance.
  8. Stage 7: Add contract-mode parity checks, tagging coverage, idempotency/error consistency, and CI/coverage gates so all Direct Connect endpoints return non-NotImplemented responses.

  2. Stage 1: Implement read/list discovery APIs (DescribeFileSystems, DescribeFileCaches, DescribeVolumes, DescribeStorageVirtualMachines, DescribeBackups, DescribeSnapshots) with deterministic seeded records.
  3. Stage 2: Implement file system/file cache lifecycle APIs (CreateFileSystem, CreateFileSystemFromBackup, UpdateFileSystem, DeleteFileSystem, CreateFileCache, UpdateFileCache, DeleteFileCache).
  4. Stage 3: Implement storage virtual machine and volume lifecycle APIs (Create/Update/DeleteStorageVirtualMachine, Create/Update/DeleteVolume, CreateVolumeFromBackup, RestoreVolumeFromSnapshot, CopySnapshotAndUpdateVolume).
  5. Stage 4: Implement backup/snapshot and copy workflows (Create/Delete/CopyBackup, Create/DeleteSnapshot, UpdateSnapshot, backup-origin and lifecycle transition state handling).
  6. Stage 5: Implement data repository association/task and S3 access-point flows (Create/Update/DeleteDataRepositoryAssociation, Create/Describe/CancelDataRepositoryTask, CreateAndAttachS3AccessPoint, DetachAndDeleteS3AccessPoint).
  7. Stage 6: Implement alias/shared-VPC operations and advanced lifecycle controls (Associate/DisassociateFileSystemAliases, UpdateSharedVpcConfiguration, ReleaseFileSystemNfsV3Locks, StartMisconfiguredStateRecovery).
  8. Stage 7: Contract hardening with deterministic pre-seeding and dependency ordering (file system -> SVM -> volume -> backups/snapshots -> repository tasks), plus docs/examples/coverage verification so all FSx endpoints return non-NotImplemented responses.
